title: Build Kasir API dari Nol
description:
Build a complete Kasir (Point-of-Sale/Cashier) REST API in Go from scratch. The API manages product data (CRUD), serves HTTP requests, returns JSON responses, and is deployment-ready.

## Goals
- Create a production-ready REST API using Go's standard library
- Implement full CRUD operations for products (Produk)
- Build a small binary (<15MB) with no runtime dependencies
- Deploy to cloud platform (Railway/Zeabur)

## API Endpoints
| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| GET | /health | Health check |
| GET | /api/produk | Get all products |
| POST | /api/produk | Create product |
| GET | /api/produk/{id} | Get product by ID |
| PUT | /api/produk/{id} | Update product |
| DELETE | /api/produk/{id} | Delete product |

## Tech Stack
- Language: Go (no frameworks, stdlib only)
- Database: In-memory (Sesi 1), SQLite (Sesi 2)
- Deployment: Railway / Zeabur

title: Define Produk Struct & In-Memory Storage
description:
Create the Produk struct to represent products and initialize in-memory storage with sample data.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Produk struct defined with proper JSON tags
- In-memory slice initialized with sample products
- All fields use appropriate Go types

## Implementation
```go
// Produk represents a product in the cashier system
type Produk struct {
	ID    int    `json:"id"`
	Nama  string `json:"nama"`
	Harga int    `json:"harga"`
	Stok  int    `json:"stok"`
}

// In-memory storage
var produk = []Produk{
	{ID: 1, Nama: "Indomie Godog", Harga: 3500, Stok: 10},
	{ID: 2, Nama: "Vit 1000ml", Harga: 3000, Stok: 40},
	{ID: 3, Nama: "kecap", Harga: 12000, Stok: 20},
}
```

## Notes
- Using int for Harga (Rupiah has no decimals)
- JSON tags ensure lowercase keys in API responses

title: GET All & POST Create Produk
description:
Implement endpoints to get all products and create a new product.

## Acceptance Criteria
- GET /api/produk returns all products as JSON array
- POST /api/produk creates new product with auto-generated ID
- POST returns 201 Created status
- Invalid POST body returns 400 Bad Request

## Implementation
```go
http.HandleFunc("/api/produk", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if r.Method == "GET" {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(produk)
	} else if r.Method == "POST" {
		var produkBaru Produk
		err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&produkBaru)
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, "Invalid request", http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		produkBaru.ID = len(produk) + 1
		produk = append(produk, produkBaru)
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
		json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(produkBaru)
	}
})
```

## Testing
```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/api/produk
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/produk -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"nama":"Kopi","harga":2500,"stok":200}'
```

title: GET Produk by ID
description:
Implement endpoint to get a single product by its ID from the URL path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- GET /api/produk/{id} returns single product
- Invalid ID format returns 400 Bad Request
- Non-existent ID returns 404 Not Found

## Implementation
```go
func getProdukByID(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	idStr := strings.TrimPrefix(r.URL.Path, "/api/produk/")
	id, err := strconv.Atoi(idStr)
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "Invalid Produk ID", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}
	for _, p := range produk {
		if p.ID == id {
			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
			json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(p)
			return
		}
	}
	http.Error(w, "Produk belum ada", http.StatusNotFound)
}
```

## Testing
```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/api/produk/1
curl http://localhost:8080/api/produk/999  # 404
```

title: UPDATE Produk
description:
Implement endpoint to update an existing product by ID.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PUT /api/produk/{id} updates existing product
- Product ID remains unchanged
- Invalid ID/body returns 400 Bad Request
- Non-existent ID returns 404 Not Found

## Implementation
```go
func updateProduk(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	idStr := strings.TrimPrefix(r.URL.Path, "/api/produk/")
	id, err := strconv.Atoi(idStr)
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "Invalid Produk ID", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}
	var updateProduk Produk
	err = json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&updateProduk)
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "Invalid request", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}
	for i := range produk {
		if produk[i].ID == id {
			updateProduk.ID = id
			produk[i] = updateProduk
			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
			json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(updateProduk)
			return
		}
	}
	http.Error(w, "Produk belum ada", http.StatusNotFound)
}
```

## Testing
```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/produk/1 -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"nama":"Indomie Jumbo","harga":4000,"stok":150}'
```

title: DELETE Produk
description:
Implement endpoint to delete a product by ID.

## Acceptance Criteria
- DELETE /api/produk/{id} removes product from storage
- Returns success message as JSON
- Invalid ID returns 400, non-existent returns 404

## Implementation
```go
func deleteProduk(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	idStr := strings.TrimPrefix(r.URL.Path, "/api/produk/")
	id, err := strconv.Atoi(idStr)
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "Invalid Produk ID", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}
	for i, p := range produk {
		if p.ID == id {
			produk = append(produk[:i], produk[i+1:]...)
			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
			json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]string{"message": "sukses delete"})
			return
		}
	}
	http.Error(w, "Produk belum ada", http.StatusNotFound)
}
```

## Testing
```bash
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/produk/1
```

title: Main Function & Routing
description:
Wire up all handlers in the main function and start the HTTP server.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All routes registered correctly
- Server starts on port 8080
- Proper routing for /api/produk vs /api/produk/{id}

## Route Configuration
| Route | Methods | Handler |
|-------|---------|---------|
| /health | GET | inline |
| /api/produk | GET, POST | inline |
| /api/produk/ | GET, PUT, DELETE | getProdukByID, updateProduk, deleteProduk |

## Key Point
- `/api/produk` (no slash) = exact match
- `/api/produk/` (with slash) = prefix match for ID routes

## Implementation
```go
func main() {
	http.HandleFunc("/api/produk/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		switch r.Method {
		case "GET": getProdukByID(w, r)
		case "PUT": updateProduk(w, r)
		case "DELETE": deleteProduk(w, r)
		}
	})
	// ... other routes
	fmt.Println("Server running di localhost:8080")
	http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil)
}
```

title: Build Binary & Deploy
description:
Build the Go binary for production and deploy to Railway cloud platform.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Binary builds successfully (<15MB)
- Production build with stripped debug info
- Cross-compilation works
- Deployed to Railway with working URL

## Build Commands
```bash
# Standard build
go build -o kasir-api

# Production (smaller ~7-10MB)
go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o kasir-api

# Cross-compile for Linux
GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o kasir-api
```

## Deploy Steps
1. Create .gitignore: kasir-api, kasir-api.exe, *.log
2. Push to GitHub
3. Go to railway.app → New Project → Deploy from GitHub
4. Railway auto-detects Go and deploys

## Verification
```bash
curl https://kasir-api-production.up.railway.app/health
```

title: Layered Architecture Refactoring

Refactor Kasir (POS) REST API from single-file in-memory to Layered Architecture with PostgreSQL database, following the Bootcamp Session 2 curriculum.

## Goals
- Implement Layered Architecture: Handler → Service → Repository → Model
- Replace in-memory storage with PostgreSQL (Supabase)
- Add config management with Viper
- Use Dependency Injection for wiring layers
- Maintain existing API contract

## Reference
- Standard Go Project Layout: https://github.com/golang-standards/project-layout
- Layered Architecture: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/PresentationDomainDataLayering.html
- Clean Architecture: https://blog.cleancoder.com/uncle-bob/2012/08/13/the-clean-architecture.html
